quirks.summary: Starting a new retrieval succeeds with 202.

evidence.summary: The operation documents 202 Accepted when a retrieval is initiated and 200 OK when the object copy was already restored, with RestoreAlreadyInProgress for a request that arrives while one is running.
Upstream shipped a default status for error codes it did not know, which is the same failure one level over: a status nobody chose reads exactly like a status somebody did.

quirks.summary: An in-progress restore header renders ongoing-request="true" with the boolean quoted.

evidence.summary: The read and head responses document x-amz-restore as an ongoing-request flag optionally followed by an expiry-date, each value in double quotes.
The date inside the header is the IMF-fixdate form HTTP fixes for every date it carries, which is what makes the embedded value byte-comparable at all.

quirks.summary: The grantee discriminator is an XML attribute of <Grantee> and not a child element, which makes it the one member of the supported surface that cannot be written by the ordinary element emitter; the frozen IR reserves xml.attributes for it and the generated encoder writes it from there rather than from a branch in the codec.

evidence.summary: Upstream had to add XML attribute support to its serializer before ACL responses could carry the discriminator at all.
The Grantee reference documents Type as an attribute of the containing element rather than as a member element.

quirks.summary: A restore of an object that is not in an archive storage class is refused 403 InvalidObjectState rather than accepted as a no-op: a caller that reads a success has no way to tell a retrieval it does not need from one that never happened.

evidence.summary: The operation documents InvalidObjectState for a request against an object whose storage class is not one of the archive classes.

quirks.summary: Type is optional in the decoded DTO because the XML reader exposes no attributes; making it required would reject every real Grantee before the runtime can derive its discriminator.

evidence.summary: The same missing capability upstream hit from the writing side; here it is the reading side that has no attribute access.
Each documented Type value pairs with exactly one identifying member, which is what makes the member a sound discriminator.

quirks.summary: The Days form requires a value of at least one.

evidence.summary: The request syntax documents Days as the lifetime of the active copy for an ordinary retrieval and as not applicable to a select-type restore, which instead carries SelectParameters and an OutputLocation.
The Days member documents a minimum value of one, so a zero-day or negative retrieval has no representable meaning.

quirks.summary: GlacierJobParameters.Tier accepts exactly Expedited, Standard and Bulk.

evidence.summary: The Tier member documents the closed value set Standard, Bulk and Expedited, and the same set appears on the request's own Tier element.

quirks.summary: The payload member is promoted to required, so a restore with an empty body is 400 MalformedXML rather than a retrieval with a duration this implementation invented: neither documented form of the request has a default, and Days in particular has none.

evidence.summary: Every documented request example carries a RestoreRequest document, and no default duration or tier is published for a request that omits it.
Upstream accepted an empty body where a document was required and answered success, and the fix pins the empty-required-XML answer to 400 MalformedXML.

quirks.summary: Unknown elements inside a RestoreRequest are skipped rather than refused.

evidence.summary: AWS ignores unknown elements in request XML, and upstream had to relax its decoder to match after strict parsing broke real clients.
The upstream fix that makes unknown request elements a skip rather than an error, which is the behaviour this decoder generates by construction.

quirks.summary: versionId selects which version of the object is retrieved, so it is decoded and carried to the handler rather than dropped: a backend that ignored it would retrieve the current version and report success for a request about another one, which is indistinguishable from having honoured it.

evidence.summary: The operation documents versionId as the query parameter naming which version of the object the retrieval applies to.

quirks.summary: The five permissions are a closed set and a grant naming anything else is refused rather than stored, which is the one place this family is stricter than its siblings: a stored permission no authorizer can evaluate is a grant that reads as present and enforces as nothing.

evidence.summary: The permissions table enumerates exactly five values and describes what each one grants on a bucket and on an object.

quirks.summary: On the way in the discriminator is derived from whichever of ID, URI or EmailAddress the grantee carries; when the unreadable attribute contradicts those members, the members decide the stored and returned type.

evidence.summary: The same missing XML-attribute capability upstream hit from the writing side; here it is the reading side that has no attribute access.
Each documented Type value pairs with exactly one identifying member, which makes the identifying member a deterministic discriminator.
